newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen's Walzdraht has more orders.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen's Walzdraht has more orders.

text.p: Walzdraht Hochfeld GmbH, the wire plant being sold to Georgsmarienhuette GmbH, may impose further price increases following improved orders to help cover 1996 losses, its parent company Thyssen Stahl AG said on Wednesday.

Thyssen Stahl said in a statement that a price increase of 30 marks per tonne would go ahead for the first quarter of 1997. The statement also said that the new orders would improve the jobs outlook at the lossmaking wire factory.
A similar price increase could also be expected from April 1, 1997, the statement added, without giving further details.
Thyssen said at the end of October it would sell Walzdraht Hochfeld and its Ruhrort steelworks to Georgsmarienhuette effective October 1, pending supervisory board approval.
The Thyssen supervisory board meets this Friday, and will also review 1995/96 results.
